links.effect: Low automation was safe/caution for >70%; high automation was probably/definitely unsafe for 30-35% across tasks.
links.quote: Notably, while low automation was consistently rated as “Safe” or “Safe with Caution” by over 70% of participants, high automation received “Probably Unsafe” or “Definitely Unsafe” ratings from 30-35% of participants across tasks (Figs. 4 and 5 ).

links.outcome: automation bias and uncritical trust concerns
links.effect: Automation bias and loss of nuance was one of five qualitative themes; participants raised concern clinicians may trust outputs uncritically.
links.quote: While many participants perceived GenAI as promising, they stressed the need for adequate trialing to ensure reliability and raised concerns about automation bias and the risk that clinicians trust system outputs uncritically.

links.effect: Preimplementation usability assessment identified five themes; workflow-improvement endorsement was IE 20/38 (54%), SUM 22/38 (59%), S2T 21/38 (57%).
links.quote: Five key themes emerged from qualitative analysis: efficiency and quality benefits; system reliability concerns; safety and medico-legal considerations; automation bias and loss of nuance; and deployment requirements including adjustable settings and oversight.

links.outcome: clinician perceived safety across documentation automation levels
